pages.text: Mom had gone to market early that morning. The sun was setting, but she was not back.
A small lamp hung on Mom's cart. "I will go to the hill to meet her." Pipo wrapped his scarf tightly and set off.
At the fork, Mrs. Goose stretched her neck. "I saw your mom! But to tell you that story, I must start with the mill family..."
She began with the mill family's story. Pipo's shadow stretched long along the road.
"That family's youngest, you see, last spring..." Mrs. Goose flapped excitedly.
Before long, the sky was dim. Pipo stamped his toes on the ground.
"...Now where was I?" She kept tilting her head.
Pipo climbed the hill. Far away, one light flickered and swayed.
A lamp! Wagging his tail, Pipo ran down toward the light.
Mom's cart approached, lamp swinging. Pipo hopped onto the seat beside her. Mrs. Goose was still tilting her head at the fork.
